We are commanded to think that there is rest for us in none of the things of the world, but, as if rising from the dead, to strive toward the heights, and to walk after the Lord our God, and to say: My soul has cleaved after you. But if we despise this, and refuse to hear him who says, Arise, you who sleep, and be lifted up, and Christ will enlighten you; we shall indeed slumber, but we shall be deceived, and we shall not find rest, for where Christ does not enlighten the one who rises, what seems to be rest is tribulation.

LXX: Because of uncleanness you have been consumed with corruption. For what we have said, you have been consumed, it can, according to the Greek understanding, sound in the Latin language as you have been corrupted, so that the order is: because of uncleanness you have been corrupted with corruption. This is said to those who, serving the pleasure of the body and lust, corrupt not only their soul but their body as well, lovers of pleasures rather than lovers of God. He could also have said, because of uncleanness you have been corrupted, and the sense would have been complete even without with corruption. But now, because he says, You have been corrupted with corruption, he seems to me to have said it to distinguish it from a salutary corruption, of which the Apostle also speaks: And though our man who is outside is corrupted, yet he who is inside is renewed from day to day. He who always carries the dying of Jesus in his body, and corrupts the outer man, and subjects the flesh to the rule of the soul, is indeed corrupted, but not with corruption, because his corruption is salutary.

LXX: You have fled with no one pursuing. This is said to those who because of uncleanness have been corrupted with corruption, that through the consciousness of their sins, even without punishments, they do not dare to resist the enemy and fight. Hence too those who are fearful in battle with the enemy, and would terrify the minds of their brothers, are cast out of the camp and driven from the battle line, and in the curses of Leviticus the word is directed to men of this kind: The sound of a flying leaf will pursue you, and you will flee, with no one pursuing. I know that I have read in the commentaries of a certain man expounding the beginning of John the Evangelist, All things were made through him, and without him was made nothing, that he referred what is said, nothing, to wickedness; and again that he interpreted wickedness itself as the devil, and by this step, as it were, understood the very nothing that was made without Christ to be the devil. If, then, wickedness, or the devil, is nothing, and those who have been corrupted with corruption fled with no one, that is, nothing, pursuing, the devil pursued them in the guise of nothing. But if this seems to anyone too forced, and argued against the simplicity of Scripture by an artifice of eloquence rather than by true interpretation, let him follow either the former exposition or one he has found himself.

[Passage quoted, Micah ii. 11.]

Micah, too, agrees with the passages from Isaiah in stating that God will not receive all without qualification, but only those who are left. And as in Isaiah "their remnant" was called "a seed," so now those of them that are to be saved are called "a drop." And the choir of the apostles is shewn forth by those figures, as being a drop and a seed from the Jewish race, a drop from which all they that have known the Christ of God through the whole world and received His teaching, have been made worthy of the congregation foretold, having obtained redemption from their enemies.
The Proof of the Gospel, Book 2, Chapter 3

LXX: The spirit has set a lie. It has dripped for you into wine and drunkenness, and it will be from the drop of this people; Jacob, to be gathered, will be gathered. It is not, as most suppose, the spirit stood false, but the spirit has set a lie that must be read, which in Greek is said πνεῦμα ἔστησε ψευδὲς, that is, τὸ ψεῦδος (the lie). For just as with putrid wounds, lest a cancer creep on and the dead body feed upon the living flesh, physicians arrest the wound and burn it with a cautery or with a καυστικῷ (caustic) powder, so the Spirit of God put an end to the lie, lest the people of God be any longer subverted by the voices of the false prophets. That spirit, in the New as well as in the Old Testament, wherever it is set down without an addition, is to be understood in a good sense, we have often said, and we shall now set it out in part, lest anyone be in doubt. But the fruit of the spirit is love, joy, peace, and: If we live by the spirit, let us also walk by the spirit, and elsewhere: But if by the spirit you put to death the works of the flesh, you will live, and in the Old Testament: Giving breath to the people which is upon it, and spirit to those who tread upon it; there is no doubt from what precedes that it signifies the earth. For those who tread on earthly works and put them under their feet surely deserve to receive not an evil but a good spirit. On the contrary, an evil spirit is always read with an addition, as there: But when the unclean spirit has gone out of a man, and in another place: He rebuked the unclean spirit, and: An evil spirit seized Saul, and other things like these. The Spirit of God, therefore, who put an end to the lie in the false prophets, will himself drip for you into wine and drunkenness: the wine that gladdens the heart of man, and the drunkenness with which Noah was made drunk, and of which it is said elsewhere: Eat, friends, and be drunk. Yet all this gladness and drunkenness, in comparison with the wisdom of God, which like a river waters the heavenly Jerusalem, is a drop and a very small droplet. Nor will those hesitate to speak of a drop of the wisdom of God in men who have read of the stone cut from the mountain without hands, and that the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and that the apostles themselves too knew in part and prophesied in part. From this wisdom, then, that is, from the drop of the Jewish people — for he came only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel —, Jacob was gathered: everyone who supplants Esau, and snatches away his birthright and blessing, and, before he is born, while still lying in the womb, seizes the heel of his hairy brother.

Would that I were not a man who has the spirit, and that I rather spoke a lie. I will drip for you into wine and into drunkenness, and this people will be the one upon whom it drips. Gathering I will gather Jacob, all of you; I will bring together into one the remnant of Israel alike. I will set him like a flock in the sheepfold, like cattle in the midst of the folds. They will be in tumult from the multitude of men; for he will go up opening the way before them; they will divide and pass through the gate and go out by it; and their king will pass on before them, and the Lord at their head. In this section too the Seventy translators differ much from the Hebrew. Therefore let us first expound according to what has been handed down to us by the Hebrews, and afterwards, if God wills, we shall treat of their translation. O Jewish people, to whom belong the promises, and whose are the covenants and the law, and from whom is Christ according to the flesh, to whom, when the Babylonians or the Romans were threatening, I said: Arise and go into captivity, since there is no rest for you in this land, which because of its uncleanness will be corrupted by a final devastation, do not think that I speak willingly and proclaim with joy what I see coming; I would wish myself to be anathema for my brothers, who are Israelites. Would that I spoke from my own mind and did not have the Holy Spirit; and that, counted rather among the false prophets, I alone might perish, and the things I say might not be true; and that so great a multitude might believe in the Son of God, and not be handed over to perpetual captivity. But since I am a prophet, and speak by the Spirit of God, and, sent by the Godhead, proclaim the truth, for this reason I will drip my word for you into undiluted wine, which will make you drunk and cause you to fall. And while I drip, and sing of the evil of the captivity to come, this people will receive my rains, that is, willing or not, it must endure what I say.

To which state and condition of sonship when we have advanced, we shall forthwith be inflamed with the piety which belongs to good sons, so that we shall bend all our energies to the advance not of our own profit, but of our Father's glory, saying to Him: "Hallowed be Thy name," testifying that our desire and our joy is His glory, becoming imitators of Him who said: "He who speaketh of himself, seeketh his own glory. But He who seeks the glory of Him who sent Him, the same is true and there is no unrighteousness in Him." Finally the chosen vessel being filled with this feeling wished that he could be anathema from Christ if only the people belonging to Him might be increased and multiplied, and the salvation of the whole nation of Israel accrue to the glory of His Father; for with all assurance could he wish to die for Christ as he knew that no one perished for life. And again he says: "We rejoice when we are weak but ye are strong." And what wonder if the chosen vessel wished to be anathema from Christ for the sake of Christ's glory and the conversion of His own brethren and the privilege of the nation, when the prophet Micah wished that he might be a liar and a stranger to the inspiration of the Holy Ghost, if only the people of the Jews might escape those plagues and the going forth into captivity which he had announced in his prophecy, saying: "Would that I were not a man that hath the Spirit, and that I rather spoke a lie;" -to pass over that wish of the Lawgiver, who did not refuse to die together with his brethren who were doomed to death, saying: "I beseech Thee, O Lord; this people hath sinned a heinous sin; either forgive them this trespass, or if Thou do not, blot me out of Thy book which Thou hast written."
The First Conference of Abbot Isaac, Chapter 18

And lest you think that I am a prophet of evils only: now indeed the foretold captivity will come; but behold, in me speaks the word of God, which comes to all the prophets. When it is silent, the prophet does not speak; and now it says: I will come, and take a human body, I will be born of a virgin. Or thus: Because I came in the humility of the flesh and you did not believe me, I will come at the consummation of the world in my majesty with the angels and the other powers, and then I will gather all of you, Jacob; then I will bring together into one the remnant of Israel, and join them alike with the people of the Gentiles in my sheepfold; then I will hedge you about with a most firm wall, and so great will be the multitude of believers, and the tumult of the flock set among the folds, that the number of the cattle will be overcome by their abundance. And lest perhaps you think, because I said, I will set him like a flock in the sheepfold, and like cattle in the midst of the folds, that I am speaking of sheep, understand that these sheep are men. For there follows: They will be in tumult from the multitude of men. Tumult is the voice of very many, and the shout of an exceedingly great multitude uttered together, so that we may not suppose it to be the voice of one, but the common voice of all, praising the good shepherd, who has leveled every steep place and made it level with his own foot, so that he, the leader of their journey, is himself the door of paradise, and says, I am the gate; and as he divides the way and goes before, being both the way and the gate, the believing flock will pass through him. And this shepherd is king and Lord. Hence there follows: And their king will pass on before them, and the Lord at their head. But if we wish to take all these things of his first coming, and to refer the whole of Jacob and the remnant of Israel to the apostles and to that multitude from the Jews which was saved in the Acts of the Apostles, the expositor's explanation will not be far from the truth. For these the Lord truly gathered into his sheepfold, and set in the midst of the folds, and made a way before them, and led them into the Church, and he was their king before them, and is the Lord at their head forever.

LXX: With all, receiving I will receive the remnant from Israel. When, he says, the people of the Gentiles has believed, and the whole world has been brought to my faith, and the fullness of the Gentiles has entered, then the remnant of Israel too will be saved; not that remnant of which it is written in the book of Kingdoms, I have left for myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal, and of which Paul speaks, So also at this present time a remnant according to the election of grace has been saved, and of which this prophet testifies above, And it will be from the drop of this people; Jacob, to be gathered, will be gathered, but that remnant which, after all have been received, will be received by God at the end, and of which it is now said, With all, receiving I will receive the remnant of Israel, so that, according to what is written, God, shutting up all under sin, may have mercy on all.

LXX: I will set their turning away like sheep in tribulation. The remnant from Israel, which I am to receive after I have received all, I will now in the meantime, because they have turned away from me, set in tribulation, and straiten, and make to sit without priest, without altar and without prophet, so that him whom they did not perceive through benefits they may understand through punishments.

LXX: Like a flock in the midst of their resting place; I will set is understood. Not only, he says, will their turning away, by which they turned away from me, be set like a flock in tribulation, but after they have been afflicted and have completed the time of distress, they will be set in rest, that is, in their resting place. And then they will migrate from men and transcend the state of the human condition, and will fulfill what follows: They will leap forth from men. And not only will they leap forth and depart, but all to whom the word of God comes, and who, leaving human vices behind, imitate the way of life of the Godhead, and hear: I said, you are gods, and all sons of the Most High, they will leap forth from men, and will be borne, as it were, to heaven.

LXX: Go up through the division. The present place has as it were its own exordium and an apostrophe of prophetic speech to him who desires to be saved, who is commanded to go up through the division. This indeed will become clearer if we take an example from Genesis, where twins are born of Tamar, with whom the patriarch Judah lay: It came to pass, it says, when she was giving birth, and had twins in her womb; in the very birth one put forth his hand, and the midwife tied scarlet on his hand, saying: This one will come out first. But when he had drawn back his hand, at once his brother came out, and she said: Why has the wall been divided for your sake? And she called his name Perez, which is interpreted division. And after this his brother came out, on whose hand was the scarlet, and she called his name Zerah, which in our language means seed, or rising. The elder people, then, in whom was the rising and the seed before the Church was born from the Gentiles, showed its hand in works, and afterwards drew it back, hearing through Isaiah: For your hands are full of blood. And when he had drawn back his hand and ceased from the works of justice, his brother, the people of the Gentiles, came out. And for his sake the hedge was divided, and the Lord and Savior destroyed, so that he might be able to advance, the partition which was in the middle and the wall separating the two peoples; and he made one flock, and created the two in himself into one new man, making peace. Hence too the midwife, speaking prophetically, says to Perez, the younger people: Why has the wall been divided for your sake? If you have understood the example from Genesis, go up, you who desire to be saved, by no means through the old people, which has its hand drawn back, but through the new, in which Christ is the way, in whom Jesus is the gate, through whom we advance to the Father; for he himself dissolved the middle partition and wall, that is, the obscurity of the ancient prophets, and opened all the mysteries of the old law, and, having scattered the difficulty of advancing, revealed the way to the eyes of all, so that whoever wishes to go on may be hindered by no obstacle nor be frightened by the fog of obscurity.

LXX: Before their face they divided and passed through the gate, and went out by it. And their king went out before their face. But the Lord is their leader. For this reason I said to you, Go up through the division, you who have risen with Christ and seek the things that are above: because the angels, or the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, divided what seemed to stand in the way, and made a way for those who wished to enter; and because, the road being open, they took to the road, they not only entered the gate, but also passed through it. And they entered because their king too entered the same gate and opened the way for them, so that they might walk without any difficulty. For the Lord himself is both king and shepherd, both the way and the gate, and he says: I am the gate: whoever enters through me will be saved; he will go in and go out, and will find pasture. Of this gate it is prophesied elsewhere too: This is the gate of the Lord, the just will enter by it. But whoever has entered ought not to remain in the state in which he entered; let him go out to the pastures, so that in entering there is the beginning, and in going out and finding pasture, the perfection of the virtues. He who enters is still in the world, and understands the Creator from the creatures. But he who goes out transcends the whole creation, and, counting as nothing all things that can be seen, will find pasture above the heavens, and will feed on the word of God, and will say: The Lord shepherds me, and I shall lack nothing. This is said so that we might understand the testimony of the Gospel, He will go in and go out, and will find pasture, and what is now said through the prophet, And they passed through the gate, and went out by it; yet this passing through and going out cannot be granted without Christ our king, who is king and Lord. For immediately there is joined: But the Lord will be the leader.
3: For the Prophets ever rebuked them, saying, "Hear, ye rulers of Sodom"; and, "Thy rulers are disobedient"; and again, "Is it not for you to know judgment?" And everywhere they attack them vehemently. What then? Shall one blame God for this? Away with the thought. This blame is theirs. And what other proof can a man bring of your not knowing the Law than your not obeying it?

LXX: And he will say: Hear these things, O princes of the house of Jacob, and the rest of the house of Israel. The sentence clings to what went before. For above he had said: But the Lord will be the leader, and he will say: Hear, O princes of the house of Jacob, and the rest of the house of Israel. For "the rest of the house of Israel", all except the Seventy translated "leaders of the house of Israel". The Lord, therefore, who made a way for his people, and went out before their face, and is himself the leader of the journey of the simpler people, whom he calls his flock, threatens those who are unwilling to follow him as he goes before, but are proud, and, as judges of the people, do not follow his footsteps, and he says: Hear, O princes of the house of Jacob, and leaders of the house of Israel. But what is it that compels them to hear? It is not yours, he says, to know judgment, you who hate the good, and seek evils; that is, you do not deserve to know the judgment of God, which is a great abyss, and the depth of his justice a perverse mind does not find. Or how can you know the judgment of God, you who hate the good and seek evil, who loathe the holy poor and honor rich sinners? And at the same time let us consider the force of the words: if not to love good things is a mark of sin, of how great a crime is it even to hate them? And on the contrary, if not to flee evil things is a fault, of how great an impiety is it even to seek them out diligently? After this the savagery of the judges is described, and their cruelty toward those subject to them.

And I said: Hear, O princes of Jacob, and leaders of the house of Israel. Is it not yours to know judgment, you who hate the good and love evil, who violently tear their skins from off them, and their flesh from off their bones, who have eaten the flesh of my people, and flayed their skin from off them; and they have broken their bones, and chopped them up as in a cauldron, and like flesh in the midst of a pot. Then they will cry to the Lord, and he will not hear them, and he will hide his face from them at that time, as they have acted wickedly in their devices. The word is plainly directed against the princes of Israel, and under the metaphor of lions or of robbers their cruelty is described: that they despoiled the poor, and killed them, and crushed their flesh and bones; and that, as in the midst of a pot, so in the city of Jerusalem they afflicted the wretched common people; and that on account of these things punishment is afterwards brought upon them in the day of captivity, whether by Nebuchadnezzar or by Vespasian and Titus. And they cry to the Lord, and he does not hear them, and he hides his face from them, because they acted wickedly in their crimes.

He delivers this address to the leaders: those entrusted with judgment trampled on justice; hence he puts it in the form of a question, Was it not you who had responsibility for judging, for punishing the guilty and letting the innocent go free without blame? How did you, then, who were entrusted with administering the laws, turn from the practice of good works and ardently support evil? You exercised such greed in regard to the needy as to strip them of all their possessions (suggesting this by saying "robbing people of their skins and the flesh from their bones").

LXX: Tearing away their skins from them, and their flesh from their bones. As they have devoured the flesh of my people, and flayed the skins from them, and broken their bones, and chopped them up like flesh in a cauldron, and like flesh in a pot; so will they cry to the Lord, and he will not hear them, and he will turn away his face from them at that time, because they have acted most wickedly in their devices. It had not been enough for them to despoil the flock subject to them, but they also afflicted their bodies with harsh rule, and crushed their bones, so as to break and grind whatever perhaps had been in them. As, therefore, they despoiled my people, and stripped them of all the beauty and comeliness of their skin, and put their flesh and bones into the boiling pot which the Assyrian king kindled, handing my flock over to the devil and his angels, so they too, when the day of vengeance has come, will cry to the Lord and will not be heard, because they themselves did not hear those who asked; and they will stretch out their hands to the Lord, and God will turn away his face from them, because they too turned away their countenance from those who entreated them. And they will suffer all these things because they acted most wickedly in their pursuits and in their pleasures; and they were not kings but tyrants, not overseers but lions, not teachers of disciples but wolves of the sheep; and they glutted themselves with flesh, and grew fat, and, like a most fat victim of slaughter, were also made ready for the punishments of the Lord. Thus far against the wicked princes; the word that follows is against the false prophets and the very wicked teachers, who trip up the people of God with flattery, promising knowledge of the Scriptures.

"The sun will go down" upon those prophets who lead my people astray, dwelling in darkness. "It will be night for you, without vision, and it will be dark for you, without dawn." "For, when [the spirit] goes out of a man, it goes about wandering." It does this quite by nature. [The Lord] rendered this judgment with regard to [the people]: "Thus will it be for this generation." That is, in the days of the prophets the evil spirit had gone out from them, [that spirit] that was sin itself.

Thus says the Lord concerning the prophets who lead my people astray, who bite with their teeth and preach peace; and if anyone does not put something into their mouth, they sanctify war against him; therefore night shall be to you instead of vision, and darkness to you instead of divination, and the sun shall go down upon the prophets, and the day shall be darkened over them, and those who see visions shall be confounded; and the diviners shall be confounded, and they shall all cover their faces, because there is no answer of God. But I am filled with the strength of the spirit of the Lord, with judgment and truth, to declare to Jacob his crime, and to Israel his sin. LXX: Thus says the Lord concerning the prophets who lead my people astray, and bite with their teeth, and preach peace over him, and it was not given into their mouth, they sanctified war against him; therefore night shall be to you instead of vision, and darkness shall be to you from divination, and the sun shall go down upon the prophets, and the day shall grow dark over them; and those who see dreams shall be confounded, and the soothsayers shall be mocked, and all these shall speak against them, because there is no one to hear them, unless I fill up strength in the spirit of the Lord, and judgment and power, to declare to Jacob his impieties, and to Israel his sins. We read that there were false prophets in Israel who for gifts preached peace, which had not been given to them, and if anyone had not given them presents, however holy he might be, they would announce to him that the wrath of God was going to come. Hence it is now said to them that they speak lies, and that their word is not prophecy but divination, and that they have not light but darkness and error. And when the things they had promised have been turned to the contrary, then they are covered with confusion, because there will not be, he says, an answer of God.

Now not even the demons will receive power to deceive them by their fraud. The oracles will be mute, the unclean spirit will be silent and will not dare to mock. So much concerning the false prophets.

But if we choose to take what is said according to the Seventy as concerning the heretics, who are truly false prophets, and say, thus says the Lord, when the Lord has not sent them, we shall not err. For they deceive the people that was once God's with error, and they do this in order to eat them, either simply in receiving presents, or mystically in the slaughter of their souls; and they promise them peace and the heavenly kingdoms, and say, there is no need for you to live continently and holily; hold the faith which we teach, and you will obtain all the promises of the Lord. Speaking such things, they rather stir up the wrath of the Lord against them, and sanctify war against them.

Wherefore, O you heretics, who think that you have prophecy and imitate the Church of God, where you suppose there is vision, there will be night, and where you boast of prophetic utterance, there the unclean spirit will speak. For the sun of justice will set upon prophets of this kind, and they will see their own darkness and be confounded. And when they have been proved to be diviners rather than prophets, they will be laughed at over their dreams, and the peoples who had formerly been deceived by them will speak against them. Then the teachers themselves too will repent, and no one will hear them except I, whom they had offended. And because I am merciful, and do not wish the death of the sinner, but desire that he turn back and live, when I have heard them I will give them the power of my spirit, and I will fill them with my judgment and strength, so that those who formerly deceived the people with blandishments may afterwards, by declaring true things, deter them and call them back to the right way, and those who had been the cause of error may begin to heal the wounds which they had inflicted, and become an occasion of health. Notice in the present passage that someone can teach after sin, provided, however, that he has washed away his former vices with worthy repentance. Hence David too, after adultery and homicide, says in the psalm: You will sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed; you will wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow. Nor is he content with his own purity alone, but he adds: Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and strengthen me with a governing spirit. And when you have done this. I will teach, he says, the wicked your ways, and the impious will be turned to you.

If, further, one works through the twelve minor prophets, many testimonies to the Holy Spirit are to be found. Thus Micah speaks as God's mouthpiece and says, "Truly I am full of power by the Spirit of the Lord." Joel cries, " 'And it shall come to pass afterwards,' says God, 'that I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh' " and what follows. Haggai said, " 'For I am with you,' says the Lord of hosts … 'my Spirit remained among you.' " And in like manner Zechariah says, "Receive my words and my statutes which I commanded my servants the prophets."

Again the speech of the prophet speaking about himself is introduced: while they prophesy falsely and are covered with confusion and ignominy, I, what I speak, I speak moved by the Holy Spirit, and I speak the judgment of the Lord and the truth. And while the false prophets bite with their teeth and preach peace, I without any fear declare to Jacob his crime and to Israel his sin, because they either worshipped idols in place of God, or crucified the Son of God.

The third ground of the influx of fortitude is from God indwelling. Whence in Micah: "I am filled with the fortitude of the Lord, with judgment and power." The human body, when it does not have a spirit, does not have power, even if it were a gigantic body; so if God is not in the soul, then it does not have power.

And all this it says will come to pass because of the sin of the house of Jacob, and the transgression of the house of Israel. And it goes on to describe this sin and transgression, "They that defile judgment and pervert all that is right, who build Sion with blood and Jerusalem with unrighteousness." With blood! Yes, this was the cause of their final misery, for that they pronounced the impious curse upon themselves, saying, "His blood be on us and on our children."
The Proof of the Gospel, Book 8, Chapter 3

The judges and princes of the house of Jacob and of the house of Israel, that is, of both the two and the ten tribes, not only did not do judgment, but abhorred it, and perverted all that is right, so that not even a little justice might remain in the city, because they built Zion with bloodshed, and Jerusalem with iniquity, with the plundering of the poor, the slaughter of the innocent, the killing of the saints.

But if anyone transfers these things which are said of Jerusalem and of Zion to the Church (for she is the house of Jacob and the house of Israel, according to what is written in Isaiah: Jacob my servant, I will uphold him, and that word to Timothy: That you may know how you ought to conduct yourself in the house of God, which is the Church), he will see clearly that the princes of the house of Jacob, and the rest of the house of Israel, or, as is better written in the Hebrew: judges of the house of Israel, are none other than the bishops, presbyters and deacons, who, unless they have kept their heart with all watchfulness, abhor judgment and pervert all that is right; for when they judge according to the person, and in the hearing of a case it is not the merit of the cause that prevails but the power of the defendants, do they not abhor judgment and pervert all that is right? But it can also be taken in another way: that the princes of the house of Jacob and the judges of the house of Israel abhor and detest judgment, turning aside from the sentence of God the judge, and distorting every rule of the Scriptures with evil interpretations; these build Zion with bloodshed, and Jerusalem with iniquity. For whereas Scripture commands: Do not bring the ungodly man into the tabernacle of the just, and: The man of blood and deceit let the Lord abhor, these, ordaining as clergy any of their hangers-on whatever, and exposing their life as a scandal to the peoples, are guilty of the unbelief of those who are scandalized. Hence it is said that it is better for a man that a millstone turned by an ass be tied around his neck and that he be cast into the deep, than that he should scandalize one of the least of the Church.

Hear these things, O princes of the house of Jacob, and judges of the house of Israel, you who abhor judgment and pervert all that is right, who build Zion with bloodshed, and Jerusalem with iniquity. Her princes judged for gifts, and her priests taught for hire, and her prophets divined for money; and they leaned upon the Lord, saying: Is not the Lord in our midst? No evils will come upon us. Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem will be like a heap of stones, and the mountain of the temple like the high places of the forests. LXX: Hear these things, O judges of the house of Jacob and the rest of the house of Israel, you who abhor judgment and pervert all that is right; who build Zion with bloodshed, and Jerusalem with iniquities. Her leaders judged for gifts, and her priests gave answers for hire, and her prophets divined for money; and they leaned upon the Lord, saying: Is not the Lord among us? No evils will come upon us. Therefore, on account of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem will be like a watch-hut for fruit, and the mountain of the Lord like a grove of the forest. No one doubts that Jerusalem was overthrown on account of the crimes which are described in this section; and since earlier the threat had gone before against either the judges or the false prophets: Hear, O princes of the house of Jacob, and leaders of the house of Israel. And after a few little verses: Thus says the Lord concerning the prophets who lead my people astray, and the rest; now the prophetic word is woven generally, both against the judges and against the false prophets, and against the priests, and against those who promised themselves the knowledge of God, and it rebukes them because on account of their crimes Zion is to be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem is to collapse like a heap of stones, and the mountain of the temple is to become like the high places of the forests. We see fulfilled the things that were said; the eyes prove the utterance of the mouth; the sight is the witness of the prophecy. This very testimony is written also in the scroll of Jeremiah, where mention is made of the prophet Micah, and the devastation of Jerusalem is foretold.

But when some of those accustomed "to pervert what is right" turn my words aside into what seems best to them, let your holiness not wonder at this. [Know] that those involved in every heresy collect from the divinely inspired Scripture as pretexts of their own divination whatever was spoken truly through the Holy Spirit, corrupting it by their own evil ideas and pouring unquenchable fire upon their very own heads. But since we have learned that some have published a corrupt text of the letter of our all-glorious father, Athanasius, to the blessed Epictetus, a letter which is itself orthodox, so that many are done harm from it, thinking that for this reason it would be something useful and necessary for our brothers, we have sent to your holiness copies of it made from the ancient copy which is with us and is genuine.

And if any of the princes seemed to judge what was right, he rather sold his sentence, and judged for gifts. The priests also did not teach the people unless they had received a price; and whereas it is said to the saints: Freely you have received, freely give, they, bringing forth the answer of God when money had been received, sold the grace of the Lord for avaricious hire. And after these evils, not understanding their sin, as though they were buying back the love of God with crimes, they kept declaring that they were judges and priests and prophets of God, and in accordance with their impenitent heart they said: The Lord is in our midst, and no evils will come upon us.

And although the prophet Malachi calls priests angels, and their mouth is the oracle of the Lord, they do not judge without the taking of gifts, though they read: Gifts blind the eyes even of the wise, and like a bridle in the mouth turn away reproof. And although it is said to the apostles: Do not possess gold and silver, nor let there be copper in your belts; and money, even when earned by labor, is to be shaken out of the hands of a holy man, they sell the words of the Lord and trade in doves in the temple. But the prophets of Jerusalem also divined for money, not knowing that prophecy is one thing and divination another; for divination is never taken in a good sense in the Scriptures. There shall be, he says, no augury in Jacob, nor divination in Israel. They seemed to themselves indeed to be prophets, but because they took money, their prophecy became divination. The apostle Peter: Silver, he says, and gold I have not; he certainly could have sold to Simon Magus what he was asking for, or rather, he could have pretended to be selling it, for the Holy Spirit can be neither sold nor bought; but he condemned the money offered, together with the one offering it. Now you may see that the prophets of Jerusalem do not have prophecy in their mouth, and rest upon the Lord, and say: No evils will come upon us, on whose account God's watchtower is cut by the enemy's plow; and the place once of peace becomes full of ruins, and the temple of the Lord is turned into briars and thorns, and is a dwelling of beasts. Nor let anyone be troubled by what we read in the first book of Kings (1 Samuel): that Saul, wishing to go to Samuel, said to his servant that he could not go to him because he did not have a price to offer for the prophecy, and that the servant answered: Behold, there is found in my hand the fourth part of a shekel of silver, and I will give it to the man of God, and he will tell us our way; for it is not written that Samuel accepted it, or that they offered it to him; on the contrary, they are fed by the prophet and invited to a meal. But suppose that he did accept it: it should be reckoned rather as offerings for the tabernacle than as payment for prophecy. For a shekel contains twenty obols, and the fourth part of a shekel is five obols. So our priests too, if they wish to sell prophecy, and to set out in their chairs the doves which the Lord overturned with a whip, let them accept five obols, not the prices of country estates. The same thing is heard also in the third book of Kingdoms (1 Kings): that the wife of Jeroboam, when her son was sick, goes to Ahijah the man of God and brings him loaves and raisins and a little jar of honey. For it is told what she brought with her, and yet it is not written that the prophet accepted it, since indeed he both rebuked her and foretold the mourning to come; although it may be that those who had been accustomed to go to soothsayers (for there were many diviners and soothsayers in Israel) thought, by a bad custom, the same thing also of the prophets, and wished to offer to holy men what they had been accustomed to offer to diviners, and that Scripture only related what they wished; yet it did not add either that they dared to offer it or that the prophets accepted it. The Apostle Paul: Those who serve the altar, he says, both partake of the altar and live. It is permitted to you, O priest, to live from the altar, not to live in luxury. The mouth of the ox that treads out the grain is not muzzled. We know these things, and yet the Apostle does not abuse this license; and having food and clothing he is content; night and day he labors with his own hands, so as not to be a burden to anyone. And he swears in his epistles that he has conducted himself holily and without avarice in the gospel of Christ, and he asserts this very thing not only of himself but also of his disciples, that he sent no one who either demanded anything from the churches or was willing to accept it. And if in some epistles he gives thanks, and calls the gifts of the senders the benevolence of God, he gathers them not so much for himself as for the poor among the saints who were in Jerusalem. Now the holy poor were those in Jerusalem who first believed in Christ from among the Jews and, cast out by their parents and kinsmen and relations by marriage, had lost both their possessions and all their household goods, which the priests of the temple and the people laid waste. If the poor are such, let them accept. But if, under the pretext of the poor, a few houses are enriched, and we eat gold in glass and earthenware vessels, then either let us change our clothes along with our treasures, or let the poor habit not seek the riches of senators. Little does it profit not to have a little linen cloth about the neck for wiping away sweat. What does it help to be μονοχίτωνας (wearing a single tunic), and to display poverty in our dress, when the whole crowd of the poor sighs for our purse?

If however circumvention occurs with a profane agreement, it is called simony, in which he who buys acquires nothing, nor does he who sells possess anything, but they only handle another's property: and this happens when a spiritual thing is sold as though it were a cheap thing. Against whom the Lord says: "Do not make my Father's house a house of trade." But some make it a den of thieves; whence: "Her princes judged for bribes, and her priests taught for hire, and her prophets divined for money."

"Sion shall be ploughed as a field, and Jerusalem shall be as a granary, and the mount of the house as a grove of the wood."

Sion and Jerusalem and the so-called "mount of the house" are what were represented before in, "And the mountains shall be shaken from beneath him, and the valleys shall be melted as wax before the fire for the iniquity of Jacob." For the mountains and the dwellers thereon were besieged for the iniquity they had wrought against Him soon and not long after Mount Sion was burned and left utterly desolate, and the Mount of the House of God became as a grove of the wood.

If our own observation has any value, we have seen in our own time Sion once so famous ploughed with yokes of oxen by the Romans and utterly devastated, and Jerusalem, as the oracle says, deserted like a lodge. And this has come to pass precisely because of their impieties, for the sake of which the Heavenly Word has come forth from His own place.
The Proof of the Gospel, Book 6, Chapter 13

Therefore, it says this, "Zion shall be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall be as a storehouse of fruit," a prophecy which was only actually fulfilled after the impious treatment of our Saviour. For from that time to this utter desolation has possessed the land; their once famous Mount Sion, instead of being, as once it was, the centre of study and education based on the divine prophecies, which the children of the Hebrews of old, their godly prophets, priests and national teachers loved to interpret, is a Roman farm like the rest of the country, yea, with my own eyes I have seen the bulls plowing there, and the sacred site sown with seed. And Jerusalem itself is become but a storehouse of its fruit of old days now destroyed, or better, as the Hebrew has it, a stone-quarry.

So Aquila says, "Therefore for your sake the land of Zion shall be ploughed, and Jerusalem shall be a quarry of stone," for being inhabited by men of foreign race it is even now like a quarry, all the inhabitants of the city choosing stores from its ruins as they will for private as well as public buildings. And it is sad for the eyes to see stones from the Temple itself, and from its ancient sanctuary and holy place, used for the building of idol temples, and of theatres for the populace.
The Proof of the Gospel, Book 8, Chapter 3

Isaiah lived almost a thousand years ago and saw Zion in its primitive form. The city was still standing, beautified with public squares and clothed in honor; yet he says, "Zion shall be plowed like a field." He was foretelling what has been fulfilled in our day. Observe the exactness of the prophecy; for he said, "Daughter Zion shall be left like a hut in a vineyard, like a shed in a cucumber patch." Now the place is full of cucumber patches. Do you see how the Holy Spirit enlightens the saints? Therefore do not be distracted by a common term but hold fast to what is exactly true.

Hence again the divine Micah was unable to brook the building of Zion with blood, however you interpret the phrase, and of Jerusalem with iniquity. Meanwhile, these heads of the house of Jacob abhorred justice. The priests were teaching for hire. The prophets were prophesying for money! What does Micah say will be the result of this? "Zion shall be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall be as a storehouse of fruit, and the mountain of the house shall be as the grove of the forest." He bewails also the scarcity of the upright, there being scarcely a stalk or a gleaming grape left, since both the prince asks and the judge curries favor, so that his language is almost the same as the mighty David's: "Save me, O Lord, for the godly man ceases." Their blessings shall fail them, for "you consume like a moth what is dear to him."
IN DEFENSE OF HIS FLIGHT TO PONTUS, ORATION 2:58

Since, therefore, they did not repent, and the whole people followed the vices of the princes and priests and prophets, Zion will be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem will be like a heap of stones, and the temple, which formerly shone with gold and silver, will collapse into utter ruins. These things are against the people of the Jews, upon whom the true captivity and the final ruins were imposed, on account indeed of their earlier crimes, but chiefly on account of the shedding of the Lord's blood. Hence too Zion has been plowed like a field, and Jerusalem turned into mounds of stones, and that temple, once noble and lofty, has been ground down into the last ashes.

Therefore, because of us, who are such, who build Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity, who judge for gifts, who give answers for hire, who divine for money, and who, claiming besides a feigned sanctity for ourselves, say: No evils will come upon us. Let us hear the sentence of the Lord which follows: Zion and Jerusalem, and the mountain of the temple, the watchtower, and the vision of peace, and the temple of Christ, at the consummation and at the end, when charity has grown cold and faith has become rare, will be plowed like a field, and will be reduced to mounds, and will be like the high places of the forests, or a watch-hut for fruit, so that where once there were spacious houses and heaps of grain without number, there there may scarcely be a little hut keeping the appearance of foods which hold no refreshment for the soul.

And there rose up men of the elders of the land and said to the whole assembly of the people, speaking: Micah of Moresheth was a prophet in the days of Hezekiah, king of Judah, and he spoke to all the people of Judah, saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Zion shall be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem shall become a heap of stones, and the mountain of the house the heights of the forests. Did Hezekiah, king of Judah, and all Judah condemn him to death? Did they not fear the Lord and entreat the face of the Lord, and the Lord repented of the evil which he had spoken against them? So we are doing a great evil against our own souls. The princes of the city and the people understand the truth of the judgment; but the elders, whose proper task it was to know old things, unfold the history and prophecy of Micah of Moresheth, who prophesied under King Hezekiah, compare it with the prophecy of Jeremiah, for which a capital charge is being pressed against him, and show that Micah had said graver things and yet had suffered nothing from the righteous king Hezekiah, but that they, converted to repentance, had turned the sentence of the Lord in a good direction. For Micah said: Zion shall be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem shall become a heap of stones, and the mountain of the house the heights of the forests; and Jeremiah: I will make, he says, this house like Shiloh, and this city I will make a curse to all the nations of the earth. And they give counsel, thinking that what Micah had foretold would by no means come to pass, because for a long time it had not been done on account of the repentance of the people, and that this too, which Jeremiah spoke, would by no means come to be, if, according to his counsel, they made good their ways and their pursuits and heard the voice of the Lord their God, so that the Lord would not bring the evil with which he had threatened them. And at the same time they break the rage of the accusers and mingle themselves with them, saying: So we are doing a great evil against our own souls, not that they ought to do it, but because, if they did it, they would by no means harm the accused, but their own souls, which they could have freed by a change of their sentence.
4:
These things are open for the eyes to see, and it should be clear as well that it is hence that the new law and word of the new Covenant of our Saviour Jesus Christ goes forth. For countless companies of people, races of all kinds deserting their fathers' gods and their old superstitions, call on the Supreme God. And thus it is reckoned the deepest peace, there being no diversity of government or national rule, that nation should not take up sword against nation, and that they should not learn war any more, but that each farmer should rest under his vine and under his fig tree, according to the prophecy, and that none should make him afraid.

As this state of things was never achieved at any other time but during the Roman Empire, from our Saviour's birth till now, I consider the proof irrefutable that the prophet refers to the time of our Saviour's coming among men.
The Proof of the Gospel, Book 8, Chapter 3

On my holy mountain, on the high mountain of Israel, says the Lord God, there all the house of Israel shall serve me: all, I say, in the land in which they shall please me; and there I will require your firstfruits and the beginning of your tithes in all your sanctifications. In an odor of sweetness I will receive you, when I have led you out from the peoples and gathered you from the lands into which you were scattered, and I shall be sanctified in you in the eyes of the nations. And you shall know that I am the Lord. Of this mountain, on which all the house of Israel is to serve God, Isaiah and Micah sang with one voice: In the last days the mountain of the house shall be manifest on the summit of the mountains and shall be raised above the hills; and all the nations shall flow to it, and many peoples shall go and say: Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord and to the house of the God of Jacob, and he will teach us his ways and we will walk in his paths; for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem; and again Isaiah: Go up onto a high mountain, he says, you who proclaim to Zion; lift up and exalt your voice, you who bring good tidings to Jerusalem. This mountain, Zion, we understand either as the Church, which means 'watchtower' and is set on the height of holy doctrines, or as the Lord Savior himself, in whom the firstfruits and the tithes and all worship are turned into an odor of sweetness, so that all the nations round about, seeing that the people of the Lord has been saved, may glorify God, and those who have been saved may know that he is the Lord.

It must also be known that the Jews and the heirs of their error refer both this section which we have now expounded and the one like it in Isaiah to the thousand-year reign of Christ and of the saints; and that what is said: All peoples shall walk, each in the name of the Lord his God, they interpret in this way: that each nation is to be tormented with its idol and sent into the fire of eternal punishment. But they are refuted by what follows: this is said not of the end of the ages but of the first coming of Christ, in which the remnant of her that halts is gathered, and the nations are saved first. Isaiah, then, set down a testimony of this kind: The word that came to Isaiah son of Amoz concerning Judah and Jerusalem: for in the last days the mountain of the Lord shall be manifest, and the house of God upon the summit of the mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills, and all nations shall come to it. And many nations shall go, and shall say: Come, let us go up into the mountain of the Lord, and into the house of the God of Jacob, and he will announce to us our way, and we will walk in it; for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. And he shall judge among many nations, and reprove a very great people, and they shall beat their swords into plows, and their hunting-spears into sickles, and nation shall not take up sword against nation, and they shall not learn to make war any more. Significantly it is said here that the word of God, going forth from Jerusalem, judges among many nations, and properly reproves the people of the Jews. For us, as sinners, he will judge according to the measure of our works; but them, as impious men and deniers, he will not judge, but will reprove them as condemned.

And it shall be in the last of days, there shall be the mountain of the house of the Lord, prepared on the top of the mountains, and lofty above the hills; and peoples shall flow to it; and many nations shall hasten, and they shall say: Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob, and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths, for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem; and he shall judge among many peoples, and rebuke strong nations even afar off; and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into mattocks; nation shall not take up sword against nation, and they shall not learn to make war any more; and a man shall sit under his vine and under his fig tree, and there shall be none to make him afraid, for the mouth of the Lord of hosts has spoken; for all peoples shall walk, each in the name of his god; but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and beyond. In that day, says the Lord, I will gather her that halts, and her whom I had cast out I will gather, and her whom I had afflicted; and I will make her that halts a remnant, and her that had labored a mighty nation, and the Lord shall reign over them in Mount Zion from this time forth and even forever. LXX: And it shall be in the last of days, the mountain of the Lord manifest, prepared upon the top of the mountains; and it shall be lifted up above the hills, and peoples shall hasten to it, and many nations shall go and say: Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord and to the house of the God of Jacob, and he will show us his way, and we will walk in his paths; for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem, and he shall judge among many peoples, and reprove strong nations even afar off, and they shall beat their swords into plows and their spears into sickles; and nation shall no more take up sword against nation, and they shall by no means learn to make war; and each shall rest under his vine, and each under his fig tree, and there shall be none to make him afraid, for the mouth of the Lord Almighty has spoken these things; for all peoples shall go, each his own way. But we will go in the name of the Lord our God forever and beyond. In that day, says the Lord, I will gather her that is crushed, and her that had been cast out I will receive, and those whom I had driven back; and I will make the crushed one a remnant, and the one driven back a strong nation, and the Lord shall reign over them in Mount Zion, from this time forth and even unto the age. Because the princes of the Jews abhorred judgment, and had perverted all that was right, and had built Zion with blood and Jerusalem with iniquity, and had not only done these things but had also judged for bribes, and the priests of Jerusalem had given answers for hire, and her prophets had divined for money, and on their account Zion had become like a plowed field, and Jerusalem had fallen into heaps of stones, and the mountain of the temple of God, made desolate, into the high places of the forests: therefore now, their house being forsaken and deserted, when the Son of God, going out of the temple, said: Arise, let us go hence, and: Your house shall be left to you deserted. The angels too, as Josephus relates, said: Let us pass over from these seats, and in place of Mount Zion the mountain of the Lord has been lifted up, of which it is said to the prince of Tyre. And you were wounded on the mountain of the Lord. But this mountain of the Lord was shown in the last of days, when the kingdom of heaven drew near. For indeed at the consummation of the ages, for the rejection of sins, our Savior appeared through his own victim, and came at the eleventh hour to hire laborers. And when his passion was accomplished, John says: It is the last hour; for in six thousand years, if five hundred years are allotted to each hour of the day, the time of the faith of the Gentiles will consequently be called the last hour. And manifest, he says, shall be the mountain of the Lord, prepared upon the tops of the mountains. He will be manifest who before had been hidden, and prepared not only on the mountains but upon the tops of the mountains, Moses and the prophets, who prophesied of him. For although all that they wrote is holy, yet in comparison with the prophecy in which they prophesied of the coming of the Savior, the rest is lowly, and by no means reaches up to the tops of the mountains. And it shall be exalted, he says, above the hills. He appeared indeed as a man, and took the form of a servant, humbled even unto death, and the death of the cross; but the Father exalted him, and gave him the name which is above every name; and the whole life of men, compared with his manner of life, is called plains and valleys. To this mountain, therefore, which is prepared upon the tops of the mountains and exalted above the hills, all peoples shall hasten, or, as it stands in the Hebrew, shall flow; that is, innumerable crowds shall gather after the manner of rivers. Now the peoples shall hasten when there believed in him alike Parthians and Medes, Elamites, and dwellers in Mesopotamia, Judea and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia, Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the parts of Libya which is near Cyrene, and visitors from Rome, Jews and proselytes, Cretans and Arabians. Do not those seem to you to have hastened to the mountain to whom it was said: Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men; and at once they followed the Savior? And again Scripture relates of James and John that, leaving the boat and their father and the waves of the world, they hastened to the mountain. And Matthew the publican, on hearing: Follow me, at once ran. That passage too in the Gospel, when great crowds followed him from Galilee and the Decapolis and Jerusalem, and Judea and beyond the Jordan, and he healed them, proves that the peoples were hastening.

After the experience of the troubles in which they would find themselves, made captive first by the Assyrians and later by the Babylonians, such a great transformation would occur regarding this place that the mountain on which God was reputed to dwell would become famous and would be shown to be superior to all the mountains and far surpass all mountains and all hills on account of the glory enveloping it as a result of the divine compassion. Large numbers from all quarters, even from foreign peoples, would hasten to assemble to reach this mountain of God, on which God is believed to dwell, and learn how they should regulate their lives and live as they ought.

The prophet Micah employed the symbol of a high mountain to speak of the gathering of the nations in Christ. He has this to say: "And it shall come to pass in the last days that the mountain of the house of the Lord shall be prepared in the top of the mountains and high above the hills; and people shall flow to it. And many nations shall come in haste, and say, 'Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths; for the law shall go forth out of Zion, and the word of the Lord out of Jerusalem. And he shall judge among many people and rebuke strong nations afar off.' "

The evangelical and divine preaching coursed to the ends of the earth, according to the Lord's prophecy contained in the sacred Gospels: "This good news will be preached to all the nations in witness to them." And he urged the holy apostles in the words, "Go, make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe everything I commanded you." This evangelical law and apostolic preaching began with Jerusalem as with a fountain and traveled across the whole world, offering irrigation to those who made their approach with faith. It is also possible to see the divine houses situated in the middle of cities, villages, fields and remote areas, conspicuous for their size and beauty, so that they are illustrious and famous even on the highest mountains.

And when the Spirit of prophecy speaks as predicting things that are to come to pass, He speaks in this way: "For out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. And He shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people; and they shall beat their swords into ploughshares, and their spears into pruning-hooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more." And that it did so come to pass, we can convince you. For from Jerusalem there went out into the world, men, twelve in number, and these illiterate, of no ability in speaking: but by the power of God they proclaimed to every race of men that they were sent by Christ to teach to all the word of God; and we who formerly used to murder one another do not only now refrain from making war upon our enemies, but also, that we may not lie nor deceive our examiners, willingly die confessing Christ. For that saying, "The tongue has sworn but the mind is unsworn," might be imitated by us in this matter. But if the soldiers enrolled by you, and who have taken the military oath, prefer their allegiance to their own life, and parents, and country, and all kindred, though you can offer them nothing incorruptible, it were verily ridiculous if we, who earnestly long for incorruption, should not endure all things, in order to obtain what we desire from Him who is able to grant it.

For Micah announced that the new law would be given in this way: "The law shall go forth out of Zion, and the word of the Lord out of Jerusalem. And he shall judge among many people, and he shall vanquish and rebuke nations." For that prior law that was given through Moses was given not on Mount Zion but on Mount Horeb. And the Sibyl showed that this would be destroyed by the Son of God. "But when all these things have been fulfilled which he spoke, at that time then the whole law is destroyed."

And while the peoples hasten, very many nations also shall go to the mountain, namely the whole world believing in him, and they shall say, calling one another to the standard of the gibbet: Come, let us go up into the mountain of the Lord. There is need of an ascent for anyone to be able to reach Christ, to the house of the God of Jacob, the Church, which is the house of God, the pillar and foundation of the truth. Moreover, that Jacob signifies the Savior we have also said above: Jacob my servant, I will receive him. And they will say this also to those to whom they had spoken: Come, let us go up into the mountain of the Lord and into the house of the God of Jacob, and they will add: That they may show us his way; understand this either of the angels who preside over the churches, or of the holy Scriptures, which show beforehand the way of the Lord, and him who says: I am the way. And let us walk in his paths, namely in the apostles, through whom we have believed in Christ. For out of Zion went forth the spiritual law, passed over to the Gentiles, the word of the Lord from Jerusalem, who will judge among many peoples.

After the experience of the troubles in which they would find themselves, made captive first by the Assyrians and later by the Babylonians, such a great transformation would occur regarding this place that the mountain on which God was reputed to dwell would become famous and would be shown to be superior to all the mountains and far surpass all mountains and all hills on account of the glory enveloping it as a result of the divine compassion. Large numbers from all quarters, even from foreign peoples, would hasten to assemble to reach this mountain of God, on which God is believed to dwell, and learn how they should regulate their lives and live as they ought.

The Father indeed has given all judgment to the Son. And he will rebuke strong nations even afar off. For the Lord catches the wise in their craftiness and has known the thoughts of the wise, that they are vain. And he discerns among the peoples who are worthy of salvation and who unworthy, and at his coming all eagerness for war will be turned to peace. Swords will be changed into plows, spears will be forged into sickles, nation will cease to war against nation. No one will learn to fight, the need of fighting being laid aside. And so great will be the rest that not only in the cities but in the hamlets too and in the fields each one will be secure; and this will come to pass because the mouth of the Lord has spoken. And first, according to the letter: before a child was born to us, whose government is upon his shoulder, the whole world was full of blood; peoples fought against peoples, kings against kings, nations against nations. In short, even the Roman Republic itself was torn by civil wars, with Cinna and Octavius and Carbo fighting; Sulla and Marius, Antony and Catiline, Caesar and Gnaeus Pompey, Augustus and Brutus, and the same Augustus and Antony, in whose battles all the kingdoms shed blood. But after Rome, with a view to the rule of Christ, obtained a single rule, the world was made open to the journeys of the apostles, and the gates of cities were opened to them, and for the preaching of the one God a single rule was established. This saying too: They shall beat their swords into plows, and their spears into sickles, can also be taken tropologically, so that we say that at the faith of Christ anger and unbridled abuse have been laid aside, so that each one puts his hand to the plow and does not look back behind him, and, breaking the darts and spears of insults, desires to reap spiritual fruits, so that, others having labored, we may enter into their labors, and it may be said of us: But coming they shall come with exultation, carrying their sheaves. Now no one fights against another, for we read: Blessed are the peacemakers. No one learns to contend to the subversion of the hearers, but he sets silence on his mouth, and is silent, because the time is evil. And each shall rest under his vine, to press the wine that gladdens the heart of man, under that vine whose husbandman is the Father, and under his fig tree, plucking the sweet fruits of the Holy Spirit, love, joy, peace and the rest. And all these things will come to pass, according to both expositions, because the words of the Lord are true, and for him to have said is to have done.

The vine, and that not in a few places, refers to the Lord himself, and the fig tree to the Holy Spirit, as the Lord "makes glad the hearts of men," and the Spirit heals them. Hezekiah is commanded to make plaster with a lump of figs—that is, the fruit of the Spirit—that he may be healed. According to the apostle this healing begins with love. For he says, "The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance." On account of their great pleasantness, the prophet calls these spiritual fruits figs. Of them Micah also says, "They shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid." Now it is certain that those who have taken refuge and rested under the Spirit and under the shadow of the Word shall not be alarmed or frightened by the one who troubles the hearts of humankind.

He is indeed the field blessed by the Lord: not this earthly one, or rough with woods, or rocky with torrents, or marshy with stagnant waters, or barren of crops, or useless for vines, or infertile with stony gravel, or gaping and dry from drought, or soaked with blood, or uncultivated with thorns and brambles: but that field, of which the Church says in the Canticles: I have adjured you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and fortitude of the field. For this is the field of which the Lord says: 'And the appearance of the field is with me'. In this field is found that grape which, when pressed, shed blood and cleansed the world. In this field is that fig tree under which the saints will rest, refreshed by the sweetness of spiritual grace. In this field is that fruitful olive tree, flowing with the ointment of the Lord's peace. In this field flourish pomegranates, which cover many fruits under the protection of one foundation of faith and nourish them with the embrace of charity.
On Jacob and the Blessed Life

However, since here in Genesis we read that paradise was planted by God in the East, and there the man whom God formed was placed; we can now find the author of this paradise. For who else could have created paradise but the all-powerful God, who spoke and things came into being, never needing those things which he desired to be generated? Therefore, he himself planted the paradise of which Wisdom says: Every planting that my Father has not planted will be rooted up. Good planting of angels, good saints. For saints are called under the fig tree and vine in that future time of peace, in which there is a type of angels.
These are the mysteries of Scripture. Who can conceive the charm of the mysteries of Sacred Scriptures of which it is said: "Every one under his vine and under his fig tree."

All peoples shall go, each in his own way, but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God unto the age and beyond. While all the nations, they say, go according to their own error, we have hastened to the mountain of the Lord, and have said: Come, let us go up into the mountain of the Lord, and into the house of the God of Jacob and we will walk in the name of Christ our Lord, for he himself is the mountain who is God.

They who are eager to go up into the mountain of the Lord and wish to learn thoroughly his ways promise a ready obedience, and they receive in themselves the glories of the life in Christ and undertake with their whole strength to be earnest in all holiness. "For let everyone," he says, "in every country and city go the way he chooses and pass his life as seems good to him, but our care is Christ, and his laws we will make our straight path; we will walk along with him; and that not for this life only, present or past, but yet more for what is beyond." It is a faithful saying. "For they who now suffer with him shall walk with him forever, and with him be glorified, and with him reign." But "they" make Christ their care who prefer nothing to his love, who cease from the vain distractions of the world and seek rather righteousness and what is pleasing to him, and to excel in virtue. Such a one was the divine Paul, for he writes, "I am crucified with Christ; and now no longer I live, but Christ lives in me." And again: "I determined not to know anything among you save Jesus Christ, and him crucified."

Now it is evident that no one can terrify or subdue us who have believed in Jesus over all the world. For it is plain that, though beheaded, and crucified, and thrown to wild beasts, and chains, and fire, and all other kinds of torture, we do not give up our confession; but the more such things happen, the more do others and in larger numbers become faithful, and worshippers of God through the name of Jesus. For Just as if one should cut away the fruit-bearing parts of a vine, it grows up again, and yields other branches flourishing and fruitful; even so the same thing happens with us. For the vine planted by God and Christ the Saviour is His people. But the rest of the prophecy shall be fulfilled at His second coming. For the expression, "He that is afflicted [and driven out]," i.e., from the world, [implies] that, so far as you and all other men have it in your power, each Christian has been driven out not only from his own property, but even from the whole world; for you permit no Christian to live.

In that day, in which the sun of justice will shine, she who had before been crushed will be gathered, and she who had been driven out will be received; and the crushed one will be gathered for this, that she may be made a remnant, and the forsaken one a strong nation. Unless indeed the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we would have been as Sodom, and we would have been made like Gomorrah. But according to the Hebrew it is beautifully put: I will gather, he says, her that halts, and her who had walked badly, and to whom Elijah had said: How long do you halt? Whose foot, which had caused stumbling, had been cut off. Her whom I had cast out, and to whom I had given a bill of divorce, I will gather; and her whom I had afflicted with various captivities, or had handed over to the devil and his angels. And lest the careful reader at once object to us: How do you assert that she who halts has been gathered, and that she who had been cast out has been collected, when the Jews remain in unbelief? Let him hear that this is said of the first Church of Christ, which believed from among the Jews, to which the apostles too belonged, concerning which Luke writes in the Acts of the Apostles that in one day three thousand believed, and elsewhere five thousand, and of whom James says to Paul: You see, brother Paul, how many thousands there are of the Jews who believe, and all these are zealots of the law. But consider also the prophetic precision: he did not say, I will make her that halts wholly saved, but I will make her that halts a remnant, so that the remnant and the elect may be saved, and her that had labored a mighty nation, namely the Christian name, which not the sword, not fires, not torments shall overcome. Look at the faith and the passion of the martyrs, and you will not doubt about the mighty nation. And the Lord shall reign over them, that is, over many nations, and over the halting remnant, in Mount Zion, in the Church, in the watchtower, in the contemplation of the virtues, from the present age and even into the future. But if anyone wishes to understand what is said: I will gather her who was crushed, and the one cast out I will receive, and the rest, of the human soul, that before the coming of Christ it served various passions and vices, and like a straying and sickly sheep was torn by the bites of wolves, he will not err, provided he knows that she who had been crushed and afflicted will afterwards be under the reign of the Lord, and will live in Zion, and is to be carried back on the shoulders of the good shepherd to her former mountain.

"And you, O tower, O cloudy shepherd of the daughter of Zion, your time shall come." These words refer to the impious king Zedekiah, whom the prophet calls "tower" because the people of Judea stayed under his shadow, and "shepherd" because of his administration of the kingdom, and "cloudy" because of the error of idolatry to which he adhered. Again, in the symbolic meaning of his words he calls the devil a cloudy shepherd, because in an allegorical sense he always attacks the daughter of Zion under a cloudy sky. And, after catching her, he drags her away from the light—indeed the one who acts maliciously hates the light. But later, the supreme and legitimate prince of the mystical Jerusalem destroyed this tyranny with his advent and drove the obscure shepherd away.

Some think that the squalid or dark tower, and the daughter of Jerusalem, are to be understood of the heavenly Jerusalem, which is the mother of the saints, of which the Apostle also says: You have come to Mount Zion, and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, which remains squalid so long as her sons are not brought back to her, and king and counselor are not in her, and pains lay hold of her as of a woman in labor, because she has given birth in vain, seeing so many sons slain.

And you, tower of the flock, cloudy one of the daughter of Zion, even unto you it shall come; and the first power shall come, the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem. Now why are you drawn together in grief? Is there no king for you, or has your counselor perished, because pain has seized you like a woman in labor. LXX: And you, tower of the flock, murky daughter of Zion, to you it shall come, and the first principality shall enter, the kingdom from Babylon of the daughter of Jerusalem. And now why have you known evils? Was there no king for you, or has your counsel perished, because pains have seized you like a woman giving birth? The tower of the flock, cloudy or squalid, which in Hebrew is called ophel, we ought to take as no other than that of which Isaiah says: And I built a tower in the midst of it, that is, of the vineyard. Now the vineyard of the Lord is the house of Israel. As long as this tower has a winepress, that is, the altar, and a wall round about, namely the help of the angels, and the devil, the boar, does not enter the vineyard, it is not squalid, it is not dark, but, having received its name from the Lord who shines upon it, it is called a city which, set on a mountain, cannot be hidden. The tower, then, once of the flock and of the people of God, because the most wicked tenants killed the son of the householder, is now squalid and abandoned, and under the name Ariel cries out from the earth in Isaiah. And this tower belongs to the daughter of Zion, or, as Symmachus rendered it into Greek: She herself is the daughter of Zion, and even unto her shall come God, or the first power, which power is the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem. Now there came to this tower the first power, or the first principality, he who had said: I am alpha and Ω, the beginning and the end, the first and the last.
